Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=draft}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=draft}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|12=draft}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=draft}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|12=draft}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=draft}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. {{日本の古墳 |名称=大和天神山古墳 |画像=[[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
航空写真 |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]柳本町 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_scale:20000|display=inline,title}} |ISO = JP-29 |形状=[[前方後円墳]] |規模=墳丘長113メートル |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=[[3世紀]]末から[[4世紀]]前半 |被葬者=不明 |出土品= |有形文化財=出土品一括（国指定）、出土木棺（県指定） |史跡指定=奈良県指定史跡 |特記事項= |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Nara|label=大和天神山
古墳|lat_deg=34|lat_min=33|lat_sec=26.0|lon_deg=135|lon_min=50|lon_sec=45.3|marksize=25|float=center|border=none|mark=前方後円墳-南.svg|position=bottom|width=200|caption=奈良県内の位置}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E}}}} }} '''大和天神山古墳'''（やまとてんじんやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]柳本町にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。奈良県指定[[史跡]]に指定されている。 == 概要 == [[行燈山古墳]]前方部の西方に位置する北向きの前方後円墳が本[[古墳]]である。[[1960年]]（昭和35年）に県道拡張工事で後円部の一部が削られたのを機会に緊急[[発掘調査]]が行われた。 本古墳は、[[伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|伊射奈岐（いざなき）神社]]境内古墳として調査が進められたが、古墳名に人名を混じらせないという方針により、地元の呼称をとって天神山古墳とされた。しかし、各地に同名の古墳が多数あるため、区別するために'''大和天神山古墳'''と命名された。 本古墳の築造時期は、周辺の古墳との関係や日本製青銅鏡の形式から、[[3世紀]]末から[[4世紀]]前半、ないしはおおむね[[4世紀]]後半とも推定されている。 == 規模・形状 == [[台地]]上に立地する墳丘長113メートルの前方後円墳で、短めの前方部はわずかに[[撥]]形に開いており、その開きは後円部の直径を超えるものではない。[[葺石]]や[[埴輪]]がなかったが、段築や周濠が不明瞭であり、本来なかった可能性も指摘されている。 == 被葬者 == 木櫃の中央部が丹念に調査されたが、遺骸を埋葬していた形跡を認めることが出来なかった。 == 埋葬施設および副葬品 == 後円部のほぼ中央に長さ6.1メートルの[[竪穴式石室]]が検出された。石室の中央部には、長さ2.6mの板材が残存しており、その中央は仕切り板で区切ってあり、内法1×0.5メートルの木櫃状になっている。 石室は自然石の小口積みで形成され、上部は石室の両側から持ち送る合掌式で、天井石を設けない型式の竪穴式石室である。 石室の内部には、一見木棺のようであるが細部を検討すると木櫃（もくひつ）とした方がよい大きな木製容器が置かれて、総重量約41キログラムの[[辰砂|水銀朱]]が納められていた。朱を大量に入手し使用している点で、3キログラムの朱を使用していた[[岡山県]][[倉敷市]]の[[楯築古墳]]があり、[[瀬戸内海]]東部との関連が考えられる。 この木櫃の底板は、長さ2.6メートル、幅75センチメートルであるが、断面は緩やかなＵ字形を呈している。しかし、巨木を刳り抜いたものではなく、縦に長い3枚の板を合わせたものである。従って内部の底面は水平でなく、両端がカーブしてあがっている。 木櫃のなかに水銀朱を取り囲むように20面の[[銅鏡]]が置かれていた。20面の銅鏡は木櫃の四周に連続して[[長方形]]の辺に置かれていて、前期古墳にしばしば見られるように一面だけ中央に置いてあるという配列とは全く異なる。古墳社会では階層化が進み、青銅鏡が社会的・政治的に重要なものであり、製作数が飛躍的に増大する林正憲「大和天神山古墳」/奈良文化財研究所(2005) 147ページ。また、木口板（こぐちいた）の外部にも北方で2面、南方で1面置かれていて、計23面の銅鏡が検出されている。 鏡種別に見ると、「尚方作竟」銘鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/008 e国宝]流雲文縁[[方格規矩鏡]]（径20.3cm）4面を含む方格規矩鏡が6面、「長宜子孫」銘鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/020 e国宝]「寿如金石佳且好兮」銘内行花文鏡（径23.7cm）を含む[[内行花文鏡]]4面、画文帯[[神獣鏡]][http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/014 e国宝]「日月天王」銘環状乳画文帯神獣鏡（径16.8cm）[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/002 e国宝]「日月天王」銘環状乳画文帯神獣鏡（径13.9cm）4面中国鏡としての方格規矩鏡・内行花文鏡は後漢代（1～2世紀）、画文帯神獣鏡三国時代（3世紀）、獣形鏡4面、画像鏡2面の合計20面が木櫃内に収められ、人物鳥獣文鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/022/001?x=470&y=1236&s=4 e国宝]人物鳥獣文鏡（径15.1cm）1面と斜縁変形神獣鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/015 e国宝]三角縁変形神獣鏡（径17.4cm）2面の計3面は木櫃外から発掘された模様である。 武器は鉄製で、刀が3点、剣が4点、鉄鏃が5点出土している。刀は一般的な片刃でなく、切っ先から20センチまで両刃になった特異なものである。 剣では木製の柄装具に直弧文この文様は呪術的文様であり、古墳時代の刀剣によく施されている。を施している。これらの剣の一部が絹布に巻かれていた。鉄鏃は、柳葉形で、木製矢柄が一部残っていた林正憲「大和天神山古墳」/奈良文化財研究所（2005）147-149ページ。 前方部から二重口縁[[壺]]（[[布留式土器|布留Ⅰ式]]）から出土している。 ==文化財== ===重要文化財（国指定）=== * 奈良県天神山古墳出土品一括（考古資料） - 明細は以下。[[奈良国立博物館]]保管。2002年（平成14年）6月26日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳出土品}}。 ** 銅鏡 23面 ** 鉄製品 16点 ** （附指定）土器片 一括 === 奈良県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 大和天神山古墳出土木棺（考古資料） - [[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所]]附属博物館保管。2008年（平成20年）3月28日指定{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf 奈良県指定文化財一覧]}}（奈良県ホームページ）。 * 史跡 ** 大和天神山古墳 - 2009年（平成21年）3月31日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *独立行政法人文化財研究所・奈良文化財研究所監修『日本の考古学－ドイツで開催された「曙光の時代」展』小学館　2005年 ISBN 4-09-681821-6 {{japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やまとてんしんやまこふん}} [[Category:山辺の道]] [[Category:柳本古墳群]] 本古墳の築造時期は、周辺の古墳との関係や日本製青銅鏡の形式から、[[3世紀]]末から[[4世紀]]前半、ないしはおおむね[[4世紀]]後半とも推定されている。 == 規模・形状 == [[台地]]上に立地する墳丘長113メートルの前方後円墳で、短めの前方部はわずかに[[撥]]形に開いており、その開きは後円部の直径を超えるものではない。[[葺石]]や[[埴輪]]がなかったが、段築や周濠が不明瞭であり、本来なかった可能性も指摘されている。 == 被葬者 == 木櫃の中央部が丹念に調査されたが、遺骸を埋葬していた形跡を認めることが出来なかった。 == 埋葬施設および副葬品 == 後円部のほぼ中央に長さ6.1メートルの[[竪穴式石室]]が検出された。石室の中央部には、長さ2.6mの板材が残存しており、その中央は仕切り板で区切ってあり、内法1×0.5メートルの木櫃状になっている。 石室は自然石の小口積みで形成され、上部は石室の両側から持ち送る合掌式で、天井石を設けない型式の竪穴式石室である。 石室の内部には、一見木棺のようであるが細部を検討すると木櫃（もくひつ）とした方がよい大きな木製容器が置かれて、総重量約41キログラムの[[辰砂|水銀朱]]が納められていた。朱を大量に入手し使用している点で、3キログラムの朱を使用していた[[岡山県]][[倉敷市]]の[[楯築古墳]]があり、[[瀬戸内海]]東部との関連が考えられる。 この木櫃の底板は、長さ2.6メートル、幅75センチメートルであるが、断面は緩やかなＵ字形を呈している。しかし、巨木を刳り抜いたものではなく、縦に長い3枚の板を合わせたものである。従って内部の底面は水平でなく、両端がカーブしてあがっている。 木櫃のなかに水銀朱を取り囲むように20面の[[銅鏡]]が置かれていた。20面の銅鏡は木櫃の四周に連続して[[長方形]]の辺に置かれていて、前期古墳にしばしば見られるように一面だけ中央に置いてあるという配列とは全く異なる。古墳社会では階層化が進み、青銅鏡が社会的・政治的に重要なものであり、製作数が飛躍的に増大する林正憲「大和天神山古墳」/奈良文化財研究所(2005) 147ページ。また、木口板（こぐちいた）の外部にも北方で2面、南方で1面置かれていて、計23面の銅鏡が検出されている。 鏡種別に見ると、「尚方作竟」銘鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/008 e国宝]流雲文縁[[方格規矩鏡]]（径20.3cm）4面を含む方格規矩鏡が6面、「長宜子孫」銘鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/020 e国宝]「寿如金石佳且好兮」銘内行花文鏡（径23.7cm）を含む[[内行花文鏡]]4面、画文帯[[神獣鏡]][http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/014 e国宝]「日月天王」銘環状乳画文帯神獣鏡（径16.8cm）[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/002 e国宝]「日月天王」銘環状乳画文帯神獣鏡（径13.9cm）4面中国鏡としての方格規矩鏡・内行花文鏡は後漢代（1～2世紀）、画文帯神獣鏡三国時代（3世紀）、獣形鏡4面、画像鏡2面の合計20面が木櫃内に収められ、人物鳥獣文鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/022/001?x=470&y=1236&s=4 e国宝]人物鳥獣文鏡（径15.1cm）1面と斜縁変形神獣鏡[http://www.emuseum.jp/detail/100041/015 e国宝]三角縁変形神獣鏡（径17.4cm）2面の計3面は木櫃外から発掘された模様である。 武器は鉄製で、刀が3点、剣が4点、鉄鏃が5点出土している。刀は一般的な片刃でなく、切っ先から20センチまで両刃になった特異なものである。 剣では木製の柄装具に直弧文この文様は呪術的文様であり、古墳時代の刀剣によく施されている。を施している。これらの剣の一部が絹布に巻かれていた。鉄鏃は、柳葉形で、木製矢柄が一部残っていた林正憲「大和天神山古墳」/奈良文化財研究所（2005）147-149ページ。 前方部から二重口縁[[壺]]（[[布留式土器|布留Ⅰ式]]）から出土している。 ==文化財== ===重要文化財（国指定）=== * 奈良県天神山古墳出土品一括（考古資料） - 明細は以下。[[奈良国立博物館]]保管。2002年（平成14年）6月26日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳出土品}}。 ** 銅鏡 23面 ** 鉄製品 16点 ** （附指定）土器片 一括 === 奈良県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 大和天神山古墳出土木棺（考古資料） - [[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所]]附属博物館保管。2008年（平成20年）3月28日指定{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf 奈良県指定文化財一覧]}}（奈良県ホームページ）。 * 史跡 ** 大和天神山古墳 - 2009年（平成21年）3月31日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *独立行政法人文化財研究所・奈良文化財研究所監修『日本の考古学－ドイツで開催された「曙光の時代」展』小学館　2005年 ISBN 4-09-681821-6 {{japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やまとてんしんやまこふん}} [[Category:山辺の道]] [[Category:柳本古墳群]] It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. ISBN 4-09-681821-6. {{japanese-history-stub}} {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a Kofun in the {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} around [[Mount Miwa]] * {{ill|Kurozuka Kofun|de}} * {{ill|Andon-yama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Shibutani-mukō mound|lt=Shibutani-mukō mound|ja|渋谷向山古墳|1=Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kushiyama Kofun|ja|櫛山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Yanagimoto Otsuka Tomb|ja|柳本大塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. ISBN 4-09-681821-6. {{japanese-history-stub}} {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a Kofun in the {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} around [[Mount Miwa]] * {{ill|Kurozuka Kofun|de}} * {{ill|Andon-yama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Shibutani-mukō mound|lt=Shibutani-mukō mound|ja|渋谷向山古墳|1=Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kushiyama Kofun|ja|櫛山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Yanagimoto Otsuka Tomb|ja|柳本大塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cinnabar|qq=}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|cinnabar|ja|辰砂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cinnabar|qq=}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}} around [[Mount Miwa]] * {{ill|Kurozuka Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}} around [[Mount Miwa]] * {{ill|Kurozuka Aerial view | location = Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture | coordinates = {{coordinates|34|33|26.0|N|135|50|45.3|E|region:JP-14_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|qq=}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|qq=}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|qq=}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised).
