It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}} around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]] * {{ill|Kurozuka Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}} around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]] * {{ill|Kurozuka Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] and [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of [[:en:Cinnabar|cinnabar]] (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six [[:en:TLV mirror|TLV mirrors]], including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} and {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|Cinnabar|en|Cinnabar|WD=Q104614|lt=cinnabar}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six {{ill|TLV mirror|en|TLV mirror|WD=Q3316102|lt=TLV mirrors}}, including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} and {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|Cinnabar|en|Cinnabar|WD=Q104614|lt=cinnabar}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six {{ill|TLV mirror|en|TLV mirror|WD=Q3316102|lt=TLV mirrors}}, including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). [[co:commons:Category:Yamato Tenjin-yama Kofun]][[ja:大和天神山古墳]] [[co:commons:Category:Yamato Tenjin-yama Kofun]][[ja:大和天神山古墳]] [[sn:commons:Category:Yamato Tenjin-yama Kofun]][[ja:大和天神山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196|1=Tenri, Nara}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}} and {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|Cinnabar|en|Cinnabar|WD=Q104614|lt=cinnabar|1=Cinnabar}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six {{ill|TLV mirror|en|TLV mirror|WD=Q3316102|lt=TLV mirrors|1=TLV mirror}}, including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196|1=Tenri, Nara}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}} and {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|Cinnabar|en|Cinnabar|WD=Q104614|lt=cinnabar|1=Cinnabar}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six {{ill|TLV mirror|en|TLV mirror|WD=Q3316102|lt=TLV mirrors|1=TLV mirror}}, including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. ISBN 4-09-681821-6. {{japanese-history-stub}} {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|qq=}} is a Kofun in the {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}} around {{ill|Mount Miwa|en|Mount Miwa|WD=Q860627|lt=Mount Miwa|1=Mount Miwa}} * {{ill|Kurozuka Kofun|de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurozuka Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Andon-yama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Shibutani-mukō mound|lt=Shibutani-mukō mound|ja|渋谷向山古墳|1=Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibutani-mukō mound|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Kushiyama Kofun|en|Kushiyama Kofun|WD=Q11544664|lt=Kushiyama Kofun|1=Kushiyama Kofun}} * {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|lt=Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|lt=Yanagimoto Otsuka Tomb|ja|柳本大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Otsuka Tomb|qq=}} == See Also == * {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}} * [[Makimuku ruins]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|大和天神山古墳|version=96036207|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{everybodywiki link|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun}} [[ceb:Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun]] [[ja:大和天神山古墳]] {{wikidata link|Q11433432}} [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Nara prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Nara prefecture]] [[Category:Prefectural Historic Sites in Nara Prefecture]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]] [[Category:Yamanobe-no-michi]] [[Category:Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Ōyamato Kofun Cluster]]

[[co:commons:Category:Yamato Tenjin-yama Kofun]][[ja:大和天神山古墳]] [[co:commons:Category:Yamato Tenjin-yama Kofun]][[ja:大和天神山古墳]] [[ja:大和天神山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] | name = Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (大和天神山古墳) | image = [[File:Yamato_Tenjinyama_kohun_aerial.jpg|280px|]]
Aerial view | location = {{ill|Tenri|WD=Q502196|1=Tenri, Nara}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.557222222222|N|135.84591666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | type = Keyhole-shaped tumulus | area = Mound length: 113 meters | burial = {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | built = Late 3rd century to early 4th century | Interred_individual = Unknown | Excavated_items = | Cultural_property = excavations (national Historic Site), wooden coffin (prefectural Historic Site) | Historic_site = Prefectural Historic Site of Nara | architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} '''Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun''' (大和天神山古墳) is a keyhole-shaped {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in Yanagimoto Town, Tenri City, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == This keyhole-shaped tumulus is situated west of the front portion of {{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}}, with its front section oriented northward. Emergency excavations were conducted in 1960 during road expansion works, which partially damaged the rear mound. The kofun was initially referred to as the Kofun within the precincts of {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|ja|伊射奈岐神社 (天理市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi Shrine (Tenri)|qq=}} but was renamed "Tenjinyama Kofun" following a local naming convention. To distinguish it from other kofun with similar names, it was officially Historic Site1 "Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun." Based on the relationships with nearby tumuli and the styles of Japanese bronze mirrors discovered, the construction period is estimated to be from the late 3rd century to the early 4th century, or approximately the latter half of the 4th century. == area and type == The tumulus is located atop a plateau, with a total length of 113 meters. The shorter front portion slightly flares out in a paddle type, but its width does not exceed the diameter of the rear circular mound. The tumulus lacks {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}} and {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, and there is no clear evidence of terracing or surrounding moats, suggesting these features might have been absent. == burial and burial goods == A vertical stone chamber measuring 6.1 meters in length was uncovered near the center of the rear circular mound. The chamber featured a wooden chest-like container (木櫃) made from large planks, partitioned in the middle, with an interior measuring approximately 1 × 0.5 meters. The chamber was constructed using a dry-laid technique with natural stones, typeing a gabled roof without ceiling stones. The wooden container held approximately 41 kilograms of {{ill|Cinnabar|en|Cinnabar|WD=Q104614|lt=cinnabar|1=Cinnabar}} (mercury sulfide). This significant quantity suggests a connection to rituals or high social status, as seen in other tumuli like the {{ill|Tatetsuki Site|ja|楯築古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatetsuki Site|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=楯築遺跡|1=Tatetsuki Site|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11541408}} in Okayama Prefecture, which contained 3 kilograms of cinnabar. The chest also contained 20 bronze mirrors arranged along its perimeter, differing from earlier layouts with a single central mirror. An additional three mirrors were found outside the chest, bringing the total to 23. The types of mirrors included: - Six {{ill|TLV mirror|en|TLV mirror|WD=Q3316102|lt=TLV mirrors|1=TLV mirror}}, including four inscribed with "尚方作竟." - Four [[Flower mirror|Flower mirrors]], including one inscribed with "長宜子孫." - Four {{ill|design-band mirrors|ja|画文帯神獣鏡|lt=wide image-band deity and beast mirror|1=Shinju-kyo|2=ja|3=神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/design-band mirrors|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with the Three Kingdoms period. - Four beast-type mirrors - Two pictorial mirrors - One person-bird-beast mirror and two triangular-edged deity-beast mirrors Weapons included three iron swords, four daggers, and five arrowheads. One of the swords featured a unique double-edged tip, while some daggers had magical motifs engraved on their wooden hilts. Additionally, textile fragments were found wrapped around some of the weapons. Ceramic burial goods included double-rimmed jars from the {{ill|Furu I type pottery|ja|布留式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furu I type pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} style. == Historic Site == === Important designation1 (National designation1) === - burial goods excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological materials): Preserved at the Nara National Museum. Designated on June 26, 2002.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|10563|奈良県天神山古墳Excavated Artifacts}} ** 23 bronze mirrors ** 16 iron burial goods ** (Accompanying Historic Site) Ceramic fragments (bulk) === Prefectural Historic Site === - Historic Site: ** Wooden coffin excavated from Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun (archaeological material): Preserved at the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute Museum. Designated on March 28, 2008.{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/ken-H27.pdf List of Historic Site Designated by Nara Prefecture]}} - Historic Sites: ** Yamato Tenjinyama Kofun: Designated on March 31, 2009. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Independent Administrative Institution for Historic Site Research and Nara designation1 Research Institute (Supervised). ''The Archaeology of Japan: The Dawn of the built.'' Shogakukan, 2005. ISBN 4-09-681821-6. {{japanese-history-stub}} {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|qq=}} is a Kofun in the {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}} around {{ill|Mount Miwa|en|Mount Miwa|WD=Q860627|lt=Mount Miwa|1=Mount Miwa}} * {{ill|Kurozuka Kofun|de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurozuka Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Andon-yama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|ja|大和天神山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Shibutani-mukō mound|lt=Shibutani-mukō mound|ja|渋谷向山古墳|1=Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibutani-mukō mound|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Kushiyama Kofun|en|Kushiyama Kofun|WD=Q11544664|lt=Kushiyama Kofun|1=Kushiyama Kofun}} * {{ill|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|lt=Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun|lt=Yanagimoto Otsuka Tomb|ja|柳本大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagimoto Otsuka Tomb|qq=}} == See Also == * {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}} * [[Makimuku ruins]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|大和天神山古墳|version=96036207|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{everybodywiki link|Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun}} [[ceb:Yamato Tenjin'yama Kofun]] [[ja:大和天神山古墳]] {{wikidata link|Q11433432}} [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Nara prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Nara prefecture]] [[Category:Prefectural Historic Sites in Nara Prefecture]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]] [[Category:Yamanobe-no-michi]] [[Category:Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:Ōyamato Kofun Cluster]]
